title: Quiz: Attribute Control Charts — p, np, c, u

questions.text: A quality engineer inspects 200 circuit boards per shift and counts the number of defective boards. The sample size is constant. Which chart should be used?
questions.explanation: The np-chart counts the number of defective items (not proportion) when the sample size is constant. Here n=200 per shift is constant, and the count of defectives is tracked.

questions.text: A website monitoring tool counts the number of broken links per webpage. Each page has a different number of links. Which chart is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Broken links are defects (one page can have multiple), and the inspection area (number of links) varies per page. The u-chart handles defects per unit with variable sample size.

questions.text: The p-chart and u-chart both use variable control limits when the sample size changes from period to period.
questions.explanation: Both the p-chart and u-chart compute UCL and LCL individually for each sample because the limits depend on the sample size nᵢ. When n varies, so do the limits.

questions.text: The c-chart and u-chart are both based on which probability distribution?
questions.explanation: The c-chart and u-chart model count data (number of defects) using the Poisson distribution, which is appropriate when counting rare events in a fixed space or time.

questions.text: An ETL pipeline processes a different number of records each day. You want to monitor the rate of invalid records. The correct chart and its centre line are:
options: c-chart, centre line = total invalid records
u-chart, centre line = total invalid / total records processed
np-chart, centre line = average records per day
questions.explanation: Invalid records are defects (not pass/fail items), and the sample size (records per day) varies. Use the u-chart. The centre line ū = total defects / total units inspected.
